global: Odd how the price of salt in {town} rose the very week the council started asking questions. A coincidence, surely.
Anyone buying iron at {gold} a bar should first ask who profits. I hear certain merchants have friends on the council.
I am told the wool trade in {town} is settling at a fair price. Fair to whom, I wonder, is a question for the next vote.
Ser, if you are haggling, do it quietly. Loud bargains draw attention, and attention draws the council's favour away from you.
I bought grain from {town} for {gold} and found a note asking for my support with it. How very thoughtful of them.
Selling horses at {gold} each is a fine way to earn coin, though I would not trust a buyer who never asks about terms.
Oh, do not mind me. I am only noting that timber prices doubled once a certain lord took the {town} granaries.
Trade is a tool like any other. Those who use it to win allies will outlast those who use it only to win coin.
Whoever wants to sell armour in {town} should come to me first. My buyers pay well and never gossip about their suppliers.
Weary of overpriced ale in every tavern. Perhaps the council should review who sets these prices before the poor go thirsty.
